title: Bessemer-backed Protectt.ai buys control of Bosch's AIShield in its first acquisition
summary: Protectt.ai acquires controlling stake in Bosch AIShield in its first major buyout
detailed: Protectt.ai has acquired a majority stake in AIShield, an AI security platform previously incubated within Bosch Global Software Technologies.
AIShield will operate as an independent company under Protectt.ai while Bosch retains a minority stake.
The acquisition integrates AIShield's AI vulnerability assessment, red teaming, and runtime guardrails into Protectt.ai to build a full-stack AI security platform.
Protectt.ai plans to expand AIShield's team from 12-15 employees to 50-60 by March 2027 to support R&D and international growth.
sentences: Cybersecurity startup Protectt.ai Labs has acquired majority stakes in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated within Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), a wholly owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH.
Protectt. ai bought into AIShield through a primary issue of fresh shares and a secondary purchase of shares from existing investors , the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
AIShield will now operate as an independent company, AI Shield Private Limited (AISW), under Protectt.ai.
Bosch will keep a minority stake, according to reports .

The fresh capital will go towards AIShield's research and development, international expansion and building what the companies call sovereign AI security capabilities, aimed at businesses and governments that want more control over where their AI systems, data and workloads sit and how they are governed.
AIShield currently has about 12-15 employees.

Protectt.ai plans to take that to 50-60 by March 2027 by hiring PhD researchers, master's graduates and engineers, and some members of its own AI security team will move to AIShield, Mimani told the publication.
He said the exact number was still being worked out.
The deal is Protectt.ai's first acquisition .
The startup set up a mergers and acquisitions team earlier this year and is looking at further acquisitions or partnerships in areas such as API security and cloud security, Mimani said.
Manish Mimani, founder and CEO of Protectt.ai, said, “ AI is moving from pilots into production across banking and regulated enterprises, and the security stack has to evolve with it.

AIShield brings a proven platform, a strong engineering team and a deep patent portfolio. ”
“ Together, Protectt.ai and Bosch aim to build India's first full-stack AI security platform, covering AI for Security, Security for AI and Sovereign AI Security, so enterprises can adopt AI confidently with the resilience and the control it demands, ” he said.
AIShield secures AI systems themselves rather than conventional software.

Its platform covers an AI model from development through production, combining security assessment and red teaming, where systems are attacked in simulation to find weak points, with runtime protection and safety guardrails.
It addresses risks specific to AI, such as prompt injection, where crafted inputs trick a model into ignoring its instructions.
BGSW launched AIShield as an autonomous corporate startup in May 2022, with more than 20 patents in AI security at the time.
It was pitched then as a SaaS product offering vulnerability assessment and protection for AI-powered devices and cloud services.

Its product line now includes AISpectra, which scans models and runs red-teaming tests before deployment, and Guardian, a firewall and set of guardrails for models and generative AI applications after deployment, according to the company .
AIShield also said it is recognised in Gartner's Market Guide for AI Trust, Risk and Security Management.
AIShield was named a CES Innovation Award honoree in 2023 for its platform and again in 2024 for its GuArdIan product , which is aimed at safe use of generative AI in enterprises.
At that time it said it served more than 40 organisations across automotive, manufacturing, banking and healthcare.
The company now has more than 40 patent filings, including 11 granted patent families, and serves customers across Europe and West Asia.
The partnership is meant to take AIShield into Asian markets through Protectt.ai's relationships in banking, financial services and insurance.
Protectt.ai was founded in 2020 by Mimani and Mohanraj Selvaraj.

It started with mobile threat defence, helping businesses protect their apps against cyber threats and fraud, and also acts as a compliance tool that helps app owners meet rules set by the RBI, SEBI and NPCI.
It now describes itself as an AI-native cybersecurity company working across mobile application security, AI security and AI-native offensive security.
Its customers include banks, NBFCs, insurers, fintechs and government platforms in India, and it has a presence in India, the UAE and the US.
Mimani said its security technology runs on more than 1 billion mobile devices and processes 15 billion mobile app sessions a month.

He expects mobile apps to rely increasingly on AI agents, with apps potentially becoming UI-less over the next one to two years, which is part of the reason the company is moving into securing AI models and agents.
Protectt.ai raised Rs 76 crore in a Series A round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in March 2025.
Bajaj Finance is also an investor, according to reports.
Mimani said the company expects to consider raising fresh funds in 2027.
Vishal Gupta, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, said the transaction reflected the growing maturity of India's technology ecosystem.
“ For investors, this is an encouraging sign of ecosystem maturity.
It demonstrates that Indian startups can create sufficient scale, credibility and market leadership to become preferred partners for global technology assets.
We expect to see more such transactions as Indian companies expand their global footprint and compete in category-defining markets, ” Gupta said.
Large security companies have been buying AI security specialists as enterprises move AI systems into production.

In July 2025, Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition of Protect AI , a US company whose capabilities include model scanning, AI red teaming, runtime protection and AI agent security, and folded it into its Prisma AIRS platform.
